Arizona Cardinals.longComment: "I'll know a little bit more as this week goes," LaFleur noted of Love, who will miss at least one more game before potentially being activated ahead of, and available for, Week 13 action. Love sustained a right high-ankle sprain Nov. 1, and at the time he was thought to be facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. However, for this coming weekend's game against the Commanders at least, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to handle Arizona's backfield duties.

Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: It's unclear how much work Branch was able to get in Monday, but his presence alone opens the door for a Week 12 return. The Falcons will provide an official update on his status when they release their first injury report of the week Wednesday.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Benford is working through a groin injury that caused him to be sidelined for Sunday's win against the Dolphins. His return to practice is encouraging, even if it was in a limited capacity, and a full session Wednesday would put the fifth-year pro on track to return for Thanksgiving Day against the Chiefs. If Benford cannot play Thursday, then the Bills would likely elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad and rotate him with Maxwell Hairston at outside cornerback opposite Davison Igbinosun.

After failing to practice in any fashion in Week 11 before sitting out Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins, Kincaid has been upgraded to a limited participant on both of the Bills' first two injury reports of Week 12. He looks to be in a good spot on the health front as Thursday's game against the Chiefs approaches, with Kincaid telling Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard after Tuesday's practice that he'll "most likely" be playing in that contest. The Bills will release their final injury report of the week Wednesday and decide whether Kincaid carries a designation into Thursday.

Williams did not play in Sunday's win over the Dolphins due to a calf injury that kept him out of all Week 11 prep. The inside linebacker's estimated presence Monday is promising, but he will likely need to suit up for on-field work Tuesday and Wednesday to get the green light ahead of Thursday night's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.
Simmons will be required to miss at least the next four games for Carolina. He's logged just six defensive snaps this season and another 206 on special teams.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Hicks was not listed on Monday's injury report, but he was unable to practice Tuesday due to a concussion. He's mostly played on special teams this season, but his absence thins the Bears' depth at safety behind starters Cam Lewis and rookie first-rounder Dillon Thieneman. Hicks' next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Johnson was considered unavailable for practice for a second straight day as he continues to nurse an ankle injury he suffered in Week 11 against the Saints. If the running back is unable to play Thursday versus the Lions, Salvon Ahmed would be a top candidate to be elevated from the practice squad for a second week in a row.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Dugger drew the questionable tag for Monday Night Football, but the veteran safety will end up missing a fourth consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury. He logged full practices during Week 11 prep, so there's a chance he makes his return in Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.

Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Though Boston played 58 of 68 offensive snaps in the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, he was managing a toe injury leading up to that contest that may have hindered his effectiveness. He was limited to just a 16-yard reception on two targets in the win over Houston and appears to still be managing the injury coming off a Week 11 bye. The Browns will post their first Week 12 injury report Wednesday, when it will be known whether Boston is still tending to the toe issue or a different health concern.

Cleveland elected to open Sanders' practice window following their Week 11 bye, giving the team up to 21 days to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. Before landing on IR on Oct. 13 due to a hip issue, Sanders carried nine times for 43 yards and added 11 receptions for 74 yards on 12 targets over five contests. He'll likely slot in behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson on the depth chart at running back once he's activated.

Burton was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans due to a calf injury that he picked up against the Saints in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to warrant an extended absence, and since he's now on IR, Burton will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 20. Since the Browns do not have another fullback on the 53-man roster, the team will likely turn to tight ends Carsen Ryan, Zaire Mitchell-Paden and Blake Whiteheart to provide blocking out of the backfield, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Moore has logged five-straight full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He would need to be activated from IR in order to be available against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. The rookie fourth-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game due to a hip injury that he sustained in training camp.

Winters upgraded to limited participation in Tuesday's practice after beginning the week as a nonparticipant. The 26-year-old has one more practice to improve his status for Thursday's game against the Eagles. DeMarvion Overshown will likely start if Winters can't play.

Mingo downgraded from his limited participation in Monday's practice to full DNP Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed the last two games due to an ankle injury and could be in danger of missing Thursday's divisional game against the Eagles if he doesn't upgrade his practice status Wednesday. KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown have been rotational options at wide receiver in Mingo's absence.

Locke logged his second straight limited practice in preparation for Week 12. The 29-year-old showed progression through two days of practice after being a DNP in all three practices in Week 11. The eight-year pro has one more chance to clear concussion protocol before Thursday's Thanksgiving game against the Eagles.

Ferguson hasn't practiced in any fashion since exiting the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. Unless he's able to mix into drills Wednesday, Ferguson will likely be sidelined for a third straight game Thursday, when the Cowboys host the Eagles in a Thanksgiving Day contest.

Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

Thompson was a full participant in practice both Thursday and Friday, but the veteran safety is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve. He'll end up missing an eighth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury he picked up in Week 3 against the Ravens. Thompson's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Jones is dealing with a hamstring injury, putting his status for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers up in the air. The rookie third-round pick has compiled eight tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games, and Tyler Onyedim would be in line for increased playing time if Jones ends up being unable to play.

Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Badie was back on the field for Tuesday's walkthrough practice, with Denver estimating him as a full participant, per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Before fracturing his thumb in the Broncos' Week 6 overtime win over the Seahawks, Badie had handled a light role out of the backfield over his five appearances on the season, carrying just six times for 22 yards to go with six catches for 67 yards. However, with RJ Harvey (knee) not yet ready to return from IR and with J.K. Dobbins (personal) serving a team-imposed suspension Week 12, Badie could find himself as the top backup to rookie Jonah Coleman if he gets activated from IR ahead of Friday's game at Pittsburgh. The Broncos will likely wait and see how Badie fares in the next two practices before deciding whether to activate him this week.

Payton didn't go into details regarding what contributed to the Broncos' decision to suspend Dobbins, but the ban comes after the veteran running back played a season-low one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders. Dobbins wasn't present for Wednesday's practice, and Payton confirmed that the 27-year-old will remain away from the team throughout Week 12 prep, per Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com. With Dobbins out of the picture for Friday's matchup with the Steelers, rookie Jonah Coleman should be in store for another hefty workload out of the backfield after breaking out for 129 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 28 touches in Week 11. Tyler Badie (thumb) was designated for return from injured reserve Tuesday and could be activated to serve as Coleman's top backup.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Clark was held out of Monday's walkthrough session while tending to a hamstring injury, but he was back on the field Tuesday in a limited fashion. His participation in Wednesday's practice will shed light on his chances of playing against the Bears on Thanksgiving Day. Rookie fifth-rounder Keith Abney, as well as Kerby Joseph and Christian Izien, would all be in line for more defensive snaps if Clark cannot play Thursday.
Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury and will miss the rest of the year. The 24-year-old rookie recorded 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks in 10 games.

Wonnum registered five solo tackles, including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. The defensive lineman may have picked up a back injury during the contest, and he will have two more chances to return to practice prior to Thursday's matchup with the Bears.

Mays missed the Lions' two prior games due to an ankle injury that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 8. His placement on IR means he's required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against Minnesota. Juice Scruggs figures to be the Lions' starting center for as long as Mays is sidelined.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Zeitler missed Green Bay's last game before the team's Week 11 bye due to ankle and triceps injuries, and it looks like his availability for Week 12 is truly up in the air. If he can't go Wednesday, the Packers could end up being perilously thin on the interior of their offensive line, as starter Sean Rhyan (ankle) and key backup Travis Glover (shoulder) are also questionable.

Rhyan sat out Green Bay's last three games before the team's Week 11 bye after suffering a high ankle sprain back in Week 7 at Detroit, and now his availability for Week 12 looks like a coin-flip proposition. If he can't suit up Wednesday, 2025 seventh-rounder John Williams may need to make another start at center against the Rams.

Glover appeared on Green Bay's injury report Monday with a shoulder issue, and it seems like he's truly questionable for Week 12. With starters Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Kevin Zeitler (triceps) also questionable, the Packers might be playing with a makeshift offensive line against a stout Rams defense Wednesday, though if Zeitler is able to go, Glover could shift to a backup role.

Moore was limited in all three practices ahead of Week 12 after re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Vikings. The 26-year-old has had a smaller role on offense since Savion Williams returned from injury, but Moore still plays a key role in the kick return unit on special teams.

Melton had a trio of limited practices leading up to the Packers' Week 12 matchup against the Rams. The 27-year-old injured his thigh in the team's Week 10 loss to the Vikings. The fifth-year pro has appeared in all 10 games for Green Bay this season, catching five of 10 targets for 34 yards.

Franklin was limited in all three practices leading up to Wednesday night's showdown against the Rams. The questionable tag is positive news for the 30-year-old linebacker, as he's missed the past four games due to a shin injury.

Parsons remains listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, but he's fully expected to play in Week 12 in what will mark his 2026 debut. The five-time Pro Bowler will be making his first appearance since tearing the ACL and meniscus in his left knee Dec. 14, 2025 and requiring season-ending surgery. Parsons has worked exclusively as a limited participant in practice since being designated for return from the PUP list Nov. 4, so the Packers could monitor his snaps closely in his first game action in more than 11 months.

Coming off a bye week, Jacobs went down as a limited participant in all three of the team's Week 12 practice sessions. While the Packers aren't closing the door on Jacobs suiting up Wednesday, head coach Matt LaFleur previously noted Sunday and Monday that the running back was still viewed as unlikely to play against the Rams. Before making a decision on Jacobs' status prior to Wednesday's 8 p.m. ET kickoff, the Packers could put him through a pregame workout to gauge if his surgically repaired right ring finger presents any issues with gripping or securing the football. If Jacobs is forced to miss a second consecutive game, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd would be in line to lead the Green Bay rushing attack for another week.

LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

Houston Texans.longComment: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the green light to play versus the Ravens, he may be part of a timeshare in the backfield or be forced to settle for No. 2 duties behind David Montgomery (groin), who returned from a four-game absence in Week 11 to run for a season-high 107 yards.

The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: In a corresponding move, Indianapolis signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster. Over the first 11 weeks of the regular season, Curry recorded 26 tackles (14 solo) including 1.0 sacks and two fumble recoveries on defense, but most of his snaps came on special teams. He'll have to miss at least the next four games as he recovers.

McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

Steichen rebuffed a report Sunday from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, who relayed that the Colts were planning to "exercise great caution" by holding Pierce out for the season as he works his way back from an aggravation of his surgically repaired heel. However, given the 3-8 Colts' place in the standings in addition to their $114 million investment in Pierce, Steichen acknowledged that the 26-year-old wideout still faces an uphill battle to make it back from IR before season's end if he's anything less than 100 percent. According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen said that Pierce currently is "doing plyometrics" and "running" after landing on IR on Sept. 26, but it's unclear how close Pierce may be to practicing.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: Tuten carried 10 times for 33 yards and recorded three receptions for 20 yards before exiting the contest with 3:40 remaining, when his ankle got stepped on for the second time that day. Though the injury was to the same ankle/foot that has resulted in Tuten being listed on the Jacksonville injury report for three straight weeks, Coen seemed to imply that the aggravation isn't viewed as a major concern. Even so, Tuten's practice activity is likely to be affected in Week 12, putting his availability for next Sunday's game against the Titans in question.
Little started the game at left tackle. Wyatt Milum has entered the game on the Jaguars' offensive line.

Jones suffered a chest injury early in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. The Jaguars will now have to operate without their top slot cornerback for the stretch run versus New York.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Smith has logged two consecutive full practices, and while he's in the league's concussion protocol, head coach Andy Reid said Tuesday that he anticipates that Smith will be available for Thursday's game against the Bills, per Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. If he's cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, then Smith would likely reclaim his starting job at right guard while Mike Caliendo reverts to a depth role.

After he had been listed as a non-participant on five straight injury reports and missed two games along the way, Walker was able to take a step forward Tuesday as he works his way back from a sore groin. Per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com, head coach Andy Reid said prior to the session that Walker was "feeling pretty good," while noting that Tuesday's practice would be important in deciding whether the running back suits up Thursday versus the Bills. Though Walker will reclaim a starting role if he ultimately gets cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, he could wind up ceding more snaps and touches to rookie Emmett Johnson, who shined as the Chiefs' lead back over the past two weeks.

VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

Norman-Lott missed Sunday's win over the Cardinals due to a knee injury. The defensive tackle was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday and logged three limited practices during Week 11 prep. The upgrade to full participation, even for an estimated practice, is a strong sign Norman-Lott will be set to suit up for Thursday night's showdown with the Bills.

Wiley was carted to the locker room in the first quarter of the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons with an ankle injury. The tight end will now be on IR as he nurses his fractured ankle until at least the latter part of the regular season. Travis Kelce, Noah Gray and Jake Briningstool are now the only tight ends on the Chiefs' active roster.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Pegues managed to log one tackle across 30 defensive snaps before exiting late in the fourth quarter. He's the third defensive lineman for the Raiders to be injured against Denver.

Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

Butler took a blow to the head late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end due to a concussion. With Tim Keenan (knee) also done for the night, JJ Pegues is the last man standing at defensive tackle for Las Vegas.

Young suffered a stinger late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Cody White is a candidate to see a slight uptick in opportunities on offense with Las Vegas.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 11, but he also endured six sacks, fumbled once and added 32 yards and one TD on his eight carries. It's unclear exactly when he picked up the head injury, but he'll be subject to the concussion protocol ahead of further game action. The Chargers take the field next Sunday against the Patriots.

Mesidor suffered an ankle injury during the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In the rookie's absence, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at outside linebacker behind starters Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack.

Mitchell temporarily exited the contest in the first half due to a back issue. However, he's since returned to the game as part of the kickoff-return unit. Mitchell is thus set to resume his usual role as both a backup RB and special-teams ace.

Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened over the weekend and appears ready to return to action Wednesday against the Packers. With all three of Steve Avila (hamstring), Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) injured, Dedich could immediately see snaps on the interior of the Rams' offensive line.

The Rams opened Turner's 21-day practice window Saturday. The defensive lineman missed the Rams' last four games while on IR due to a groin injury he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. Given his ability to participate in full Monday, there appears to be a good chance he will be activated ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.
The Rams' left guard was injured in Week 9 against the Commanders and will miss a second straight game. Bill Murray or Justin Dedich (undisclosed) projects to start in Avila's place versus Green Bay.

McMahon suffered a knee injury during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. The injury is severe enough for McMahon to require a stint on IR, so he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, with his next chance to play being Week 16 against the Seahawks on Christmas Day. With Coleman Shelton nursing a hamstring injury, the Rams may have to turn to other options like David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer to fill in at center for the time being.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.

Brents didn't return to Sunday's loss to the Bills after sustaining a shoulder injury. The 26-year-old is still expected to undergo further tests but appears to have avoided anything serious. Brents has 36 tackles (21 solo) and two pass deflections through 10 regular-season games.

That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Addison injured his thumb during a Week 10 practice and was sidelined for the Vikings' Nov. 15 win over the Packers before undergoing surgery this past week. He remained out for Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers and looks headed for a third straight absence this weekend, but Addison avoided placement on injured reserve and could have a realistic chance at returning to action in Week 13. Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton are likely to be the main beneficiaries from playing-time standpoints while Addison is unavailable.

Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

New England Patriots.longComment: New England won't publish its next injury report until Wednesday, but Brown seems unlikely to practice in any capacity this week after head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't anticipate the wideout playing this Sunday against the Chargers. Assuming Brown ends up being ruled out for the Week 12 contest, the Patriots will be left with Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams as its main options at receiver.

The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

Doubs, who last suited up Week 6, is eligible to return from injured reserve at any point, but Vrabel's comments suggests that the wideout isn't a lock to be reinstated ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers. With fellow wideout A.J. Brown (hamstring) unlikely to play Week 12 and potentially set to miss additional time beyond that, a prominent role in the passing attack could be available for Doubs once's he ready to play. However, Doubs will eventually make his return to an offense missing Drake Maye (fibula), with Tommy DeVito in line to replace Maye as the team's starting quarterback beginning this Sunday.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: The Saints expect to have a better feel for Johnson's status Wednesday, when the team holds its first practice of Week 12. Before exiting Sunday in the third quarter, Johnson was targeted just once and failed to record a reception for the second time in 10 appearances on the season. If the hamstring injury prevents Johnson from playing next weekend in Cincinnati, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps at tight end.

New York Giants.longComment: Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

New York Jets.longComment: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: It seems like Ebiketie might have suffered the injury during Sunday's game versus the Steelers. Regardless, his availability for Philadelphia's game against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving is now in question. If he's unable to practice Wednesday, his odds of playing Thursday will probably be low.

Mitchell injured his left hamstring during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday. He was held out of Monday's walkthrough practice but was back on the field in a limited capacity Tuesday, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio told reporters that Mitchell should "be fine" to face the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Riq Woolen would be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Mitchell cannot play Thursday.

Shipley remained limited for a second day in a row while dealing with an illness and a foot injury. The running back returned to action in Week 11 after missing four games with a foot injury, and the illness is likely the more substantial concern at the moment. Shipley will have one more chance to be a full participant at Wednesday's final session ahead of Thursday's matchup with the Cowboys.

Jones suffered an ankle injury during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday. Philadelphia didn't hold practice Monday, so his participation over the next two sessions will shed light on his chances of playing against Dallas on Thanksgiving Day. Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was also injured in Week 11, so the Eagles could very well have Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo as the outside cornerbacks against a Cowboys offense that scored seven touchdowns (four passing, three rushing) in a 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.

Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Dunker has put together four consecutive full sessions since being designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday. The rookie third-rounder is in the final stages of his recovery from an MCL sprain that he sustained in September. Dunker would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Friday's game against the Broncos.

Herbig upgraded his DNP practice status from last week to limited participation Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed Week 11 due to a hip injury. He has two more practice sessions to increase his chances of playing Friday against the Broncos.

The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.

The Steelers haven't yet brought Pittman back from injured reserve, but he stands a good chance at being activated for Friday's game against the Broncos. Pittman was listed as a full participant Tuesday on a third consecutive practice report, as he works to regain conditioning after missing the Steelers' last six games.

Highsmith recorded a pair of sacks across just six snaps before he was forced out in the first quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles due to the ankle injury. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Steelers' initial belief is that Highsmith's ankle injury isn't serious, but the edge rusher will nonetheless have difficulty getting clearance to play on a short week. If healthy, Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) -- who was inactive for Week 11 -- will be the most likely candidate to start in place of Highsmith on Friday.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: McKivitz was carted off the field after going down with the injury during the second quarter, when Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace appeared to roll up on back of McKivitz's left leg at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run. Assuming follow-up tests confirm the injuries, McKivitz will require surgery and will almost certainly miss the remainder of the regular season and playoffs. Vederian Lowe came off the bench to replace McKivitz at right tackle, and Shanahan confirmed that Lowe will be next in line to start at the position beginning with the 49ers' Week 12 matchup with the Seahawks.

Lenoir played in Week 11 despite working through a foot injury that was sustained in Week 9 against Las Vegas. The issue didn't seem to slow the 27-year-old against the Vikings, as he played 81.0 percent of defensive snaps, which was within his usual range.

The veteran cornerback remains on injured reserve but had been listed as questionable. He had his 21-day practice window opened 17 days ago, so the 49ers will need to make a decision on Hobbs next week. He's yet to play in a game this season.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Darnold has been sidelined for the Seahawks' last two games due to a quad issue and a cracked rib, but he was back on the field Monday for a bonus practice coming out of the bye week. While Macdonald relayed that Darnold "looked great"  and took "a ton of reps" during what the coach referred to as more of a walk-through session, the Seahawks want to see how the veteran quarterback responds to a full-speed practice Wednesday before giving him the green light to start Week 12. After leading the Seahawks to their second Super Bowl championship in 2025, Darnold has endured a rough start to 2026, completing 60.2 percent of his passes and posting a 10:9 TD:INT while missing nearly four full games due to injury.

Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Lucas exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. The right tackle appears to have sustained a significant injury and likely will not return to the contest. Josh Jones should finish the game at right tackle for the Seahawks.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.

Parrish exited Sunday's Week 11 game against the Lions after sustaining a back injury. The 22-year-old has played in nine games in 2026, recording 40 tackles (33 solo) and 14 pass deflections, including two interceptions.

Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Tennessee Titans.longComment: Moore may have picked up the injury during the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. James Hudson figures to take over at left tackle in Moore's absence.

Burgess injured his knee early in the second half, and he will be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. He was filling in for Tony Adams (illness) at safety, so Isaiah Oliver is the next man up for the Titans.

Flott was hurt with just under six minutes remaining in the first half while tackling CeeDee Lamb. He was evaluated on the sideline and subsequently deemed questionable to return. Micah Robinson entered at cornerback in Flott's stead.

Adams was added to the Titans' injury report right before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff due to the illness, and the veteran safety wasn't able to take any snaps before being ruled out for Sunday's contest. Terrell Burgess drew the start at safety alongside Kevin Winston in Adams' absence, per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Robertson suffered an ankle injury at the team's final practice of the week, so his absence Monday comes as no surprise. In his absence, Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin will both likely operate in more prominent roles at cornerback versus Cincinnati.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
